embeds.title: 🔴 New CIFSwitch Linux Flaw Gives Root on Multiple Distributions
embeds.description:
A newly discovered local privilege escalation vulnerability dubbed 'CIFSwitch' in the Linux kernel allows attackers to forge CIFS authentication key descriptions and gain root privileges. The flaw impacts multiple Linux distributions including Linux Mint 21.3/22.3, CentOS Stream 9, Rocky Linux 9, AlmaLinux 9, Kali Linux 2021.4–2026.1, and SLES 15 SP7. The vulnerability was discovered by Asim Viladi Oglu Manizada, a SpaceX security engineer, and has been fixed by a kernel patch that adds validation of cifs.spnego request origins.
**Sources:** BleepingComputer • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** none • **Access:** local
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** claim
[Read source](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/new-cifswitch-linux-flaw-gives-root-on-multiple-distributions/)
